evidence_sources.object: The thread challenges bitrate-only inferences, asks for controlled tests and notes network congestion, but it does not test either candidate speaker.

evidence_sources.object: A directional label alone does not establish uniform response or quality because off-axis dispersion, lobing, distortion, sensitivity and room interaction are separate performance dimensions.
evidence_sources.subject: 360-degree speaker claim

accepted_phrases: A 360-degree label is not by itself proof of uniform or superior sound; off-axis dispersion, lobing, distortion, sensitivity, frequency response, and the listening environment still matter.

evidence_sources.object: The file-format definition concerns source resolution, while a wireless codec can still be lossy; the label alone does not prove the full Bluetooth path.
evidence_sources.subject: hi-res audio label

accepted_phrases: High-resolution audio refers to source bit depth and sample rate; a hi-res label does not by itself establish a lossless end-to-end Bluetooth path.

evidence_sources.object: The X supplies no particulate-protection rating, while water digit 7 refers to temporary immersion under defined pressure and time, up to one meter for 30 minutes in the cited table.
evidence_sources.subject: IPX7 rating

accepted_phrases: IPX7 is a bounded temporary-immersion classification, not unlimited waterproofing; X means no particulate-protection level was assigned from the available data.

evidence_sources.object: LDAC remains lossy and its default best-effort bitrate changes with connection strength, so a high-resolution source label alone does not establish delivered wireless fidelity.
evidence_sources.subject: LDAC Bluetooth path

accepted_phrases: LDAC is a lossy Bluetooth codec whose best-effort bitrate changes with connection strength, so codec support and operating conditions are part of any wireless hi-res claim.

evidence_sources.object: It is a tuned enclosure-pressure mechanism that can help reproduce deep pitches, but the label alone does not establish bass quality or transient performance.
evidence_sources.subject: passive radiator

accepted_phrases: A passive radiator is a real tuned enclosure mechanism that can assist low-frequency output, but its presence alone does not prove superior bass quality.

evidence_sources.object: Participants connect speaker preference to bass, bodily sensation, listening position, comfort and accuracy; the thread is not about either candidate and does not validate water use.
evidence_sources.subject: one general speaker-preference thread

evidence_sources.object: Electrical watts do not alone establish perceived loudness or clean maximum output; efficiency and allowed distortion matter, and a Max figure is not equivalent to a continuous rating.
evidence_sources.subject: portable-speaker wattage

accepted_phrases: A portable speaker's watt figure is electrical power, not direct proof of loudness or clean maximum output; efficiency, continuous-versus-maximum measurement, and allowed distortion matter.

generator_view.scenario: A buyer has a hard $60 budget and wants one portable speaker for a balcony and occasional poolside use. They distrust headline wattage and distortion-free marketing.
generator_view.target: Audit the physical meaning and evidence limits of the listed wattage, distortion, 360-degree, passive-radiator, IPX7, battery, and hi-res-over-Bluetooth claims, then choose the better-supported route under the stated priorities.

query_requirements.text: Compare the prices and exact output, distortion, battery, water, and radiation-pattern wording in both product listings.

Give one auditability-first recommendation that depends on every necessary evidence branch and states the measurement and real-world-validation caveats.

research_subgoals.description: Compare both frozen product listings and interpret their wattage and distortion disclosures under the same measurement context.
Separate physically real design mechanisms from unsupported quality inferences for passive radiators, 360-degree sound, and hi-res Bluetooth claims.
Interpret IPX7 within its test scope and distinguish general community discussion from same-model pool or beach validation.
Apply the auditability-first priority to all verified branches, choose one speaker, and preserve every material limitation.

Passive radiators and dispersion are real design concepts, but those labels do not prove superior bass or uniform 360-degree response; a hi-res label also does not prove a lossless or stable Bluetooth path.
The Soundcore Flare 2 costs $53.49, specifies 20W as two 10W channels, and lists THD+N below one percent, although the captured listing does not state the THD test condition.
Both listings claim IPX7, which is bounded temporary immersion; the captured community threads do not provide same-model pool or beach validation for either candidate.
